key_insight: A foundation model-based MIL pipeline for H&E whole-slide cervical biopsy screening generalized well across five countries, with Athena showing the best overall HSIL detection performance and the most consistent results.
clinical_relevance: If validated further, this approach could support more reliable high-grade cervical lesion triage in diverse settings and help reduce variability in pathology review.
method: Compared Athena with four pathology foundation models: H-optimus-0, Hibou-L, Midnight-12k, and Virchow.
Evaluated binary HSIL detection on H&E whole-slide images from Portugal, Cambodia, Germany, Poland, and Scotland.
Benchmarked model performance against trained pathologists on a p16-confirmed dataset.
evidence_signal: Athena achieved the highest mean AUC (0.931) with the lowest cross-country variability (STD 0.022), and improved sensitivity to 95% while keeping specificity comparable to pathologists (85% vs. 84%).
watch_item: Cross-country performance was strong, but boundary-case errors between low-grade and high-grade lesions show that deployment still needs careful local validation and quality control.
paper_title: Cross-country generalizability of foundation models for cervical cancer screenings on H&E whole slide images
